pins.kicker: Sunset is an hour earlier now
pins.title: Set a turnaround time
pins.sub: Check today's sunset, plan to be back at the car an hour before it, and turn around when half your time is gone, wherever you are.

pins.title: What to wear
pins.sub: Start a little cool, and add a layer the moment you stop.

pins.kicker: Cold hike in a cotton hoodie?
pins.title: Swap it for fleece
pins.sub: Cotton soaks up sweat and stays wet, so you chill fast at the top. Fleece dries quicker and keeps much of its warmth when damp.

pins.title: Loosen the laces
pins.sub: Boots laced too tight squeeze your feet and slow warm blood. Leave room to wiggle your toes, wear wool socks and pack a dry spare pair.

pins.title: Keep your filter warm
pins.sub: Freezing can damage many hollow-fiber water filters without any sign. Sleep with it in your bag and carry it in an inside pocket.

pins.title: Why carry a bivy
items: Waiting is when you get cold
A bivy blocks wind and wet
It folds small in any daypack
pins.sub: An emergency shelter, not a sleeping bag. Still wear your warm layers inside it.

pins.kicker: Hiking with your dog in the cold
pins.title: Dog winter checks
items: Short coat? Think about a dog jacket
Check paws for ice between the toes
Bring water for the dog too
Keep the leash on near ice

pins.title: Plan a cold day hike
items: Pick a short trail you know
Pack traction if it froze overnight
Turn back if the trail turns icy

pins.title: Hike after the frost
pins.sub: 22 pages on layering, short daylight, traction and cold-weather warning signs, plus checklists in °F and °C.
